Cache keys MUST include request-varying parameters — failure causes cross-request data leakage

No-refund on tool execution error — refunding enables quota bypass via deliberate error-induction (GHSA-hcq5)

competing_interpretations.interpretation: The 5-platform split (Vercel+Railway+Convex+Cloudflare+Tauri) is a deliberate 'right tool for each job' architecture — each platform owns a role no other platform can cover
evidence: WebSocket relay requires persistent connection → Railway (Vercel Edge is request-response only)
User state + billing + webhooks require transactional DB → Convex (Redis can't do transactions)
Edge CORS short-circuit requires Cloudflare Worker (Vercel middleware adds latency)
Desktop local API requires in-process Node.js (Tauri sidecar, can't call cloud for offline)

competing_interpretations.interpretation: The hand-rolled Convex distributed lock is technical debt — Convex's transactional primitives could likely express the same invariant, but the author either didn't know or chose TTL locks for simplicity
evidence: TTL-based locks have classic failure modes (lock holder crash → wait until TTL expiry; TTL too short → lost updates)
Convex's transactional model is designed for exactly this kind of multi-step atomic operation
No comment explaining why Convex transactions were insufficient

competing_interpretations.interpretation: Token-overlap and NLU solve different problems: token-overlap solves 'precise routing to known tools', NLU solves 'semantic mapping of unknown intent'. The 'transparency' comparison conflates two different axes
evidence: Token-overlap is white-box debuggable for developers but invisible to API callers
NLU can output routing rationale in natural language (user-facing transparency)
Token-overlap deterministically fails on out-of-vocabulary intent; NLU probabilistically succeeds

challenge_record.target: MCP anonymous/authenticated method split (#4937) is non-negotiable
challenge_record.counter_evidence: If anonymous methods required auth: agent-readiness scanners (and MCP SDK initialize handshake) would 401, then hang 30s waiting for the transport that never responds. If gated methods were anonymous: Pro quota bypass (unlimited free tool calls).
challenge_record.notes: The split is genuinely load-bearing — both directions of violation break the system. The 30s SDK timeout is a protocol-level constraint, not a tunable. mcp-live-smoke.yml 6-hourly cron confirms the invariant holds in production.

challenge_record.target: No-refund on tool execution error (GHSA-hcq5) is necessary
challenge_record.counter_evidence: If refunds were given on error: a Pro token could drive unlimited upstream cost by (a) always exceeding the output budget (sunk cost is real, refund is free), or (b) driving calls that reliably error after the costly upstream fetch. Both bypass the 50/day cap. The no-refund rule converts the daily cap from 'advisory' to 'enforced'.
challenge_record.notes: This is user-hostile in the benign case (user hits a transient error, loses a slot) but architecturally necessary in the adversarial case. The tradeoff is explicit in code comments — a deliberate security-vs-UX decision.

challenge_record.target: Hand-rolled Convex distributed locking is necessary
challenge_record.counter_evidence: At high concurrency: (1) lock holder crash → wait until TTL expiry (lost write); (2) TTL too short → concurrent writes after lock expiry; (3) no fencing token → stale lock holder can write after its lock expired. Convex's native transactional model is designed for exactly this use case and avoids all three failure modes.
challenge_record.notes: The lock may be technically debt rather than necessity. Without an ADR explaining why Convex transactions were insufficient, this looks like 'roll your own' where a platform primitive exists. Confidence weakened but not overturned — there may be an undocumented reason (e.g., cross-shard transaction cost).

challenge_record.target: 4-layer cache hierarchy is necessary for 65+ upstream providers
challenge_record.counter_evidence: If Redis removed: every request hits upstream directly. 65+ providers with rate limits (typical 100-1000 req/min) would be exhausted within minutes under dashboard load. The seed-meta freshness tracking is the only thing preventing the dashboard from serving stale data silently — without it, staleness is invisible.
challenge_record.notes: The 4-layer hierarchy is genuinely load-bearing. Redis is the single coalescing point — its failure cascades to upstream rate-limit exhaustion. The stale-if-error directives in bootstrap.js cache headers provide graceful degradation for transient Redis failures, but a sustained outage would be catastrophic.

challenge_record.target: Per-domain Edge Function bundling (20× cold-start reduction) is worth the self-containment constraint
challenge_record.counter_evidence: At 35+ proto services, the self-containment constraint (no cross-dir imports) means shared helpers must be duplicated or kept in api/_*.js underscore-prefixed helpers. The constraint prevents accidental cold-start bloat but adds friction for code reuse. The 20× figure is claimed in a comment but not benchmarked in the repo.
challenge_record.notes: The constraint is enforceable and enforced (tests + pre-push hook). The 20× claim is plausible (esbuild tree-shaking per-function vs mega-function bundle) but unverified. The friction is real but manageable via the _*.js helper convention.

challenge_record.target: Token-overlap concierge routing is preferable to NLU
challenge_record.counter_evidence: Token-overlap's transparency is developer-facing (white-box debuggable), not user-facing (API callers can't see the score). NLU can output routing rationale in natural language. Token-overlap deterministically fails on out-of-vocabulary intent; NLU probabilistically succeeds. The two solve different problems: precision routing vs semantic mapping.
challenge_record.notes: The 'transparency' claim was modified from absolute to qualified: token-overlap is more transparent for developers debugging known-tool routing, but NLU is more transparent for users understanding why a tool was selected. The deterministic-fail vs probabilistic-succeed tradeoff is a real design choice, not a clear win.

design_space.chosen: Multi-platform split — each platform owns a role no other can cover
rejected: Single Vercel backend (can't do WebSocket relay or transactional user state)
Single Railway backend (can't do edge compute with global CDN)
Vercel + Convex only (no WebSocket relay for AIS stream, no edge CORS short-circuit)
Self-hosted on Docker/GHCR only (loses edge compute, adds ops burden)
design_space.why_chosen: Each platform covers a capability gap the others can't: Railway for persistent WebSocket, Convex for transactional state, Cloudflare for edge CORS, Tauri for offline desktop, Vercel for edge compute + CDN
design_space.why_rejected: Single-platform options each miss at least one capability; the 5-platform split is the minimal covering set
design_space.tradeoff: Operational complexity (5 platforms to monitor, 20+ CI workflows) vs capability coverage

design_space.decision: Proto-contract (sebuf) gateway generation vs hand-written handlers
design_space.chosen: Proto definitions → buf generate → TypeScript client/server stubs + OpenAPI specs
rejected: Hand-written TypeScript handlers with manual types (no contract enforcement)
OpenAPI-first with codegen (no RPC semantics, HTTP-only)
GraphQL schema (overkill for request-response RPC, adds query complexity)
design_space.why_chosen: Single source of truth: proto/ defines service → generates client + server + OpenAPI + docs. CI enforces freshness (proto-check.yml). sebuf.http.config annotations map RPCs to HTTP verbs.
design_space.why_rejected: Hand-written loses contract enforcement; OpenAPI-first loses RPC semantics; GraphQL adds complexity for a request-response model
design_space.tradeoff: Proto toolchain learning curve + buf dependency vs single-source-of-truth contract enforcement

design_space.decision: Per-domain Edge Function bundling vs mega-function
design_space.chosen: Each api/<domain>/ is a separate Edge Function, esbuild-bundled per file, self-contained
rejected: Single mega-function (all routes in one bundle — simple but cold-start loads everything)
Catch-all routing ([...path].ts) — loses per-domain bundling
design_space.why_chosen: 20× cold-start reduction (claimed) — Vercel bundles only one domain's code per function. Enforced by tests/edge-functions.test.mjs (no node: imports, no cross-dir imports) + pre-push esbuild check.
design_space.why_rejected: Mega-function simpler but cold-start loads all 35+ services; catch-all loses the bundling benefit
design_space.tradeoff: Self-containment constraint (no cross-dir imports, shared helpers in _*.js) vs cold-start performance

design_space.decision: Hand-rolled Convex distributed locking vs Convex transactional primitives
rejected: Convex native transactional model (multi-step atomic operations)
External lock service (Redis-based Redlock, etcd)
design_space.why_chosen: No documented rationale in code or ADR. Likely chosen for simplicity (TTL locks are easy to reason about) or unfamiliarity with Convex transactions.
design_space.why_rejected: Unknown — no ADR explaining why Convex transactions were insufficient
design_space.tradeoff: TTL lock failure modes (crash recovery, fencing) vs simplicity

design_space.chosen: Bootstrap seed → in-memory → Redis → upstream (4-layer) + seed-meta freshness tracking
rejected: 2-layer: in-memory → upstream (simple but no cross-instance coalescing)
3-layer: in-memory → Redis → upstream (no seed-meta freshness visibility)
CDN-only (no Redis, rely on CDN TTL — no stampede protection)
design_space.why_chosen: 65+ upstream providers with rate limits require stampede protection (cachedFetchJson coalesces concurrent misses). Seed-meta enables health endpoint freshness alerts. 4 layers give graceful degradation (stale-if-error).
design_space.why_rejected: Simpler caches either lack stampede protection (2-layer) or freshness visibility (3-layer) or cross-instance coalescing (CDN-only)
design_space.tradeoff: 4-layer complexity + Redis as SPOF vs survivability under 65+ provider load

design_space.decision: No-refund on tool execution error (GHSA-hcq5) vs refund-on-error
design_space.chosen: No-refund — once tool._execute() runs, daily slot is charged for good
rejected: Refund on any error (user-friendly but enables quota bypass via deliberate error-induction)
Refund only on pre-execution failures (already implemented — reservation/validation failures don't charge)
Partial refund based on upstream cost (complex, hard to verify)
design_space.why_chosen: Refunding let Pro token bypass daily cap by driving calls that reliably error after the costly upstream fetch. No-refund converts cap from advisory to enforced.
design_space.why_rejected: Refund-on-error is user-friendly in benign case but architecturally broken in adversarial case; partial refund is unverifiable
design_space.tradeoff: User UX (lose slot on transient error) vs security (quota cannot be bypassed)

design_space.chosen: Token-overlap scoring (name hits 3x, description hits 1x, deterministic ordering)
rejected: NLU engine (semantic intent mapping, natural language routing rationale)
Vector embedding similarity (semantic but black-box)
Manual routing table (explicit but rigid)
design_space.why_chosen: Deterministic, white-box debuggable, predictable for agent-to-agent routing. Name weighting prevents 'chokepoint status' routing to shipping-mentioning tools.
design_space.why_rejected: NLU is black-box and non-deterministic; vector embedding is black-box; manual table is rigid and doesn't scale to new tools
design_space.tradeoff: Precision on known tools (token-overlap) vs recall on unknown intent (NLU). Token-overlap deterministically fails on out-of-vocabulary intent.

design_space.decision: 3-tier auth-aware bootstrap cache policy vs uniform policy
rejected: Uniform no-store (safe but no CDN benefit for public data)
Uniform public cache (dangerous — authenticated user data leaks into CDN)
Single public tier (loses the on-demand freshness distinction)
design_space.why_chosen: Public data benefits from long CDN TTLs; authenticated data must never be cached (privacy + freshness). On-demand tier is a middle ground for less-critical public data.
design_space.why_rejected: Uniform policies either lose CDN benefit or risk data leakage
design_space.tradeoff: CDN hit rate (public) vs data privacy/freshness (authenticated)
